observations.summary: A repository test passed while asserting the opposite of the contract named in its own comment. Mutating the --fail-on-drift exit expression so the gate fails every clean sweep left all 16 tests green, so a broken opt-in gate would have shipped behind a green Gate A.

success_criteria: Mutating a contract predicate that a test names causes at least one test in the repository suite to fail, demonstrated by running the mutation.
The check derives its subjects rather than reading a hand-kept list, so a newly added contract enrolls without editing the checker.
Every existing suite and Gate A step stays green under the unmutated tree, with no test weakened to accommodate the check.
The change playbook rule that currently scopes mutation proof to validator rules is restated to cover any newly asserted contract, or the narrower scope is defended in writing.

monitoring_plan.criterion: After promotion, a deliberate mutation of a covered contract predicate continues to fail at least one test, and Gate A remains green on the unmutated tree.

lesson.reason: No control has been designed. The candidate shapes are a Gate A mutation step, a targeted mutation corpus, or a wording change to the change playbook; choosing among them is the first attempt's work and belongs to the named owner, not to this observation.

disposition_reason: Recorded at observed. A recurring normalized fleet failure with one precisely evidenced instance and one documented prior occurrence qualifies for a typed record under the improvement lifecycle. No attempt has been made, no control designed, and no promotion is claimed or authorized by this record.
limitations: The earlier occurrence is known only from AGENTS.md prose and has no incident record, so the recurrence claim rests on one precisely evidenced instance plus that documented prior.
The observation source is added in the same commit as this record, so source.revision is null; no prior revision binds it.

Severity high reflects consequence if unfixed rather than realised impact: the defect was caught by adversarial review before merge, but a false-green test undermines every other claim the fleet's gates make.
The semantic improvement validators are parked at tag pre-trim-2026-08-02, so only the schema layer of this record is enforced today; its lifecycle legality is a written contract, not a checked one.
Gate A was green throughout the incident and is not implicated: it is structural by design and never asserted this contract.
